dimensions.name: Knowledge Delta
dimensions.justification: Adds concrete expert knowledge: exact price differentials (e.g., ~20% Graviton discount), decision‑matrix thresholds (EngineCPU <20% for right‑sizing), break‑even formulas for Serverless, RN exchange mechanics, data‑tiering cost reduction (~45%), and specific node‑type pricing numbers. This information goes beyond what a generic model already knows.

dimensions.name: Mindset + Appropriate Procedures
dimensions.justification: Provides an AWS‑specific procedural flow: pre‑flight data collection, validation steps, ordered CLI commands, snapshot before change, one‑dimension‑per‑maintenance‑window, and RN exchange steps. Minor gap: does not explicitly spell out a verification step for Redis‑module ARM compatibility before a Graviton migration.

dimensions.name: Anti-Pattern Quality
dimensions.justification: Contains a thorough NEVER list with concrete reasons (e.g., never downsize Redis based only on CPUUtilization, never drop replicas below one for HA, never migrate to Graviton without module check). Missing a few edge‑cases such as forgetting to adjust security groups or parameter groups after node‑type changes.

dimensions.name: Specification Compliance
dimensions.justification: Full front‑matter, clear description of WHAT it does, WHEN to invoke, activation triggers, invocation schema, and a minimal valid input example. No missing required fields.

dimensions.name: Progressive Disclosure
dimensions.justification: Information is layered (quick start, mindset, step‑by‑step, anti‑patterns, navigation) allowing agents to skim or dive deeper. However, the initial sections are dense and present many details up front, creating some cognitive overload before the user reaches the concise top‑level contract.

dimensions.name: Freedom Calibration
dimensions.justification: Calibrates freedom precisely: destructive actions require CONFIRM, snapshots, one‑dimension‑per‑window, batch size limits, and safety gates. No over‑constraining of creative tasks.

dimensions.name: Pattern Recognition
dimensions.justification: Follows a recognizable pattern (description → contract → mindset → ordered steps → anti‑patterns → navigation). Slightly ad‑hoc in naming sections (e.g., “Quick start” vs “Mindset”) prevents a perfect score.

dimensions.name: Practical Usability
dimensions.justification: Provides decision trees, concrete CLI commands, savings calculations, and error‑gate handling. Missing are explicit examples of handling regional pricing variations for Serverless and a fallback example when a CLI command fails (e.g., retry logic). These gaps reduce practical execution confidence, so 2 points are deducted.
